title: QUIC RFC 9000 Timer-Gated Path MTU Discovery Work Item
summary: Integrate the existing DPLPMTUD helper with the connection runtime using a bounded timer-gated probe that safely validates common Ethernet datagram sizes before ordinary traffic uses them.
planned_changes:
- Keep ordinary path traffic at 1200 bytes until a matching PMTU probe is acknowledged.
- Arm a dedicated PMTU timer only after application stream data is acknowledged.
- Send one exact PING-plus-PADDING probe only on an idle, still-current validated path.
- Cap IPv4 and IPv6 Ethernet targets by peer max_udp_payload_size.
- Promote active, candidate, or recently validated path state only on a matching acknowledgment.
- Remove outstanding DPLPMTUD state on loss without promoting the path ceiling.
- Add focused path-size, timer, packet-shape, acknowledgment, and recovery-regression proof.
- Validate the candidate with adjacent local HTTP/3 baseline/candidate evidence before ProtocolLab confirmation.
verification_plan: Run focused S14P3 and recovery/timer tests, run the broader timer/recovery/metrics filter, execute matched local HTTP/3 A/B/B/A and control campaigns, validate SpecTrace JSON, run the Release build and full Release suite, and check the diff.
out_of_scope: Repeated PMTU probe search and retry backoff.
Public or ranked performance claims before matched ProtocolLab confirmation.
Changes to authentication, congestion control, flow control, loss recovery, or fairness rules.
completion_notes: Implemented the timer-gated probe integration after rejecting three trigger placements that interfered with recovery or ACK-transition behavior. The final local candidate passed focused correctness and matched HTTP/3 performance gates with zero workload failures.
